paper.description: Page ground. Inverts to #17140e in dark theme.

card.description: Product cards, inputs, empty states. Inverts to #201c14 in dark.

kraft.description: Masthead, bin rail, spec-table keys, scrollbar track. Inverts to #241f15 in dark.

kraft-deep.description: Skeleton fill, pressed/hover grounds. Inverts to #2c261a in dark.

ink.description: Primary text, object borders, active nav fill, band chip outline. Inverts to #f0ece2 in dark.

ink-soft.description: Secondary text, mono captions, meta lines. Inverts to #b4ac97 in dark.

line.description: Quiet 1.5px borders and dashed dividers. Inverts to #8a8068 in dark.

drawer.description: Assistant card ground. #1a1a1a light, #0d0b07 dark — deepens rather than inverts.

drawer-ink.description: Text on drawer. #f0ece2 in both themes.

band-brown.description: Digit 1; laptops category; light-theme scrollbar thumb.

band-red.description: Digit 2; ADD control; error border/dot; input caret; stock 'bin empty'.

band-yellow.description: Digit 4; low stock dot; text-selection highlight; and, as a filled control, human-only actions (Yellow-Is-Human rule).

band-grey.description: Digit 8; fallback band for undecodable digits.

band-white.description: Digit 9. Text on white bands flips to ink.

band-gold.description: Tolerance metal, no digit value. Reserved for tolerance bands.

band-silver.description: Tolerance metal, no digit value. Reserved for tolerance bands.

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-copy: nav, fields, legends, buttons. Tracking widens as size drops (0.08em–0.26em).

mono.purpose: Every number and machine trace: SKU, bin code, search, tool-trail.

price.purpose: Printed money: JetBrains Mono 700, 19px, tabular-nums, beside its magnitude tick.

motion.name: money-at-rest
motion.purpose: Prices render static; the per-digit band decode was retired with the digit strips — motion is reserved for live state (typing dots, countdowns).

browserSurface.name: caret
browserSurface.purpose: Red caret in all inputs and textareas.

browserSurface.name: scrollbar
browserSurface.value: width/height 12px; track var(--kraft); thumb var(--color-band-brown) with 3px kraft border, 8px radius (dark: thumb var(--line))

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Catalog grid goes 2-up; masthead extras appear.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Bin rail docks at 248px; desktop nav; rail legend appears.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Assistant docks as sticky 400px right column.

narrative.overview: ShopMind is a working electronics shop that reads like its own inventory. The palette is not a mood board — it is the IEERC ten-band resistor ladder, the same color code every engineer decodes on a component's body. Categories, stock levels, and price digits arrive as band chips on paper label cards, filed in kraft bins, inked in near-black. Depth and hierarchy come from tonal grounds (paper, card, kraft, ink) and hairline-precise borders, never from gradients or shadows. The single most load-bearing fact of the system: exactly one color is not data. Yellow, in filled-control form, is the human-action marker — the visual proof of the Assist invariant that the AI quotes and only a person pays. The type pairing reinforces the fiction: Archivo, a sturdy grotesque worn in tight uppercase caps with wide tracking, does the shelf-label voice; JetBrains Mono, tabular, does every number.
keyCharacteristics: The resistor color ladder *is* the palette; every band carries real data (category, stock, or a price digit).
Grounds are packaging material — paper, kraft cardstock, ink drawer — not accents.
One non-data color: yellow as a filled control means "human only."
Flat by construction: 1.5px solid outlines and tonal steps convey all depth; zero shadows, zero gradients.
Bands never decode alone: the digits are always printed beside them.
Dark mode inverts the grounds warm; band colors keep their exact identity.

rules.name: The Ten-Band Rule
rules.body: The ladder is the entire accent palette. No new accent colors enter the system; anything that encodes data picks a band, and anything that isn't a band is a ground.

rules.name: The Yellow-Is-Human Rule
rules.body: Yellow in filled-control form marks actions only a human may take. The assistant's surface may *show* a yellow link ("Review bill") but no yellow control may be one the agent can press, and no pay action renders inside chat. The bin-rail legend states this in words; the system states it in color.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Band Rule
rules.body: Text on any band uses ink (#1a1a1a), with the single exception of category corner tabs, which use card-white on saturated bands (and flip back to ink on band-white). Never white-on-yellow.

rules.name: The Digits-Beside-Bands Rule
rules.body: Every band encoding prints its digits or a text label alongside the chips — prices show the mono figure beside the magnitude tick, stock shows a word ("in bin · 7"), the legend spells the code out. A band alone is never the only carrier of a value (colorblind fallback, fixed).

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: All money, quantities, and counts render in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums. Prose never sets numbers in Archivo.

rules.name: The Flat-Outline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stack by material color and border weight only. If a screen needs to feel "above" another, it changes ground (card on paper, kraft on card) or border color (line → ink), never elevation. Hover deepens borders and brightens fills (brightness), it does not lift.

dos: Do encode data only with ladder bands, and print the digits beside every encoding (magnitude tick + mono figure; stock dots + "in bin · 7").
Do keep all 1.5px borders — solid for real edges, dashed for frames, dividers, and awaiting-content states.
Do reserve yellow filled controls for actions a human must take across the money boundary; surface them in assistant contexts only as links *to* human-only pages.
Do set every number in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums, and every label in uppercase Archivo with tracking widened as size drops.
Do let band colors ride both themes unchanged; only grounds (paper, card, kraft, ink, line, drawer) invert, and the dark inversion stays warm (#17140e ground, #f0ece2 ink), never blue-grey.
Do keep money static at rest — the digit-by-digit price-strip decode left with the strips; motion is reserved for live state (typing dots, expiry countdowns).
Do theme the browser surface with the world: dashed ink focus ring (2px, 3px offset), yellow selection on ink text, red caret, kraft scrollbar track with a brown (light) or line (dark) thumb.
Do ship loading, empty, error, and partial states on every surface, and let the empty photo plate say "photo not on file."
donts: Don't put a pay or charge control inside the assistant panel or chat — the capability does not exist in the agent's tool surface and the UI must not fake it.
Don't reuse one band for two categories, or introduce an accent color outside the ladder and the grounds.
Don't use shadows, gradients, or glass effects; depth is tonal.
Don't render white text on yellow, or any band text that isn't ink (the card-white category-tab exception aside).
Don't show a band encoding without its printed digits — the color carries flavor, never sole meaning.
Don't rename "ShopMind" or spell the world's categories in lowercase; the shelf-label register is fixed.
